mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility over the past two weeks indicates a gradual return to office work, which will drive an increase in RETAIL_REC as people spend more time near their workplaces for shopping and leisure over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES showing a consistent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in PARKS mobility, especially after a period of relative stability, suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure activities, leading to a decrease in overall discretionary spending and thus lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases, even though PARKS mobility dropped by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility show a concurrent upward trend, it signifies a broader return to urban activity and commuting, creating a synergistic effect that boosts RETAIL_REC significantly over the next four weeks due to increased foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing week-on-week increases.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions, an increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are staying home more, directly correlating with reduced outings for non-essential retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated in a tightening restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: A recent sharp decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests a general reduction in essential errands, which often precedes or accompanies a decline in discretionary retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility showing a significant recent decline.

mechanism_narrative: When RETAIL_REC mobility drops below a critical threshold of -55% from baseline, it often triggers a 'bounce-back' effect as consumers seek out deals or return to activities, leading to a rebound and higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days continues to decline or stagnate after falling below -55% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of unfavorable weather (implied by declining PARKS mobility) combined with increased RESIDENTIAL activity, people are less likely to engage in outdoor or out-of-home retail, leading to a decrease in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS decreases while RESIDENTIAL increases week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite PARKS decreasing and RESIDENTIAL increasing week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, even a slight week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility indicates growing confidence and a return to normal routines, which will translate to an immediate, albeit small, increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases, despite WORKPLACES showing a week-on-week increase in a reopening regime.
